metadata.title: GEEK Protocol — Kaspa node diagnostics
metadata.schema: correctIndex is zero-based; options contains four distinct strings
metadata.reviewNotice: Internal review of the pinned Rusty Kaspa implementation. No current-network or universal API capability claim. Advanced node diagnostics remain outside introductory Study; independent editorial review is unassigned and difficulty is provisional.
metadata.attribution: Original Geek Protocol questions referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa sources; no source prose or code imported.

questions.prompt: In Rusty Kaspa's process metrics, how does resident_set_size differ from virtual_memory_size?
options: Resident physical memory versus the process's virtual-memory usage
Available disk space versus the size of the node log
Total host RAM versus the number of CPU cores
Confirmed wallet funds versus pending wallet funds
questions.funFact: The monitor documents resident memory separately from virtual memory. A large virtual-memory figure is not automatically the same amount of physical RAM in use.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: In Rusty Kaspa's I/O display, what distinguishes disk_io_read_bytes from disk_io_read_per_sec?
options: Disk writes versus disk reads
A byte count versus a read rate in bytes per second
Network traffic versus disk traffic
Transaction fees versus an account balance
questions.funFact: The display formats the first value with B and the second with B/s. A quantity and its rate have different units and should not be treated as interchangeable.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: A Rusty Kaspa Borsh metrics sample has many connection attempts but few live connections. What do these measurements distinguish?
options: Synchronized peers from orphan transactions
Accepted blocks from unsuccessful proof-of-work hashes
Currently active connections from recorded connection attempts
Outbound peers from all connected peers
questions.funFact: The service maps live connections to active_connections and attempts to total_connections. An attempt count does not say that the same number of clients are connected now.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: For Rusty Kaspa's BandwidthMetrics, what does the tx/rx distinction describe?
options: Transactions accepted and rejected by consensus
Database bytes retained and pruned
CPU threads running and waiting
Bytes sent and received, separated by the listed transport
questions.funFact: The service reads transmit and receive byte counters separately for Borsh wRPC, JSON wRPC, P2P and gRPC. Here tx labels transmitted traffic, not a count of confirmed transactions.

questions.prompt: What errors does Rusty Kaspa's ResolveFinalityConflict RPC handler return in safe mode and with unsafe RPC enabled?
options: UnavailableInSafeMode in safe mode; NotImplemented with unsafe RPC enabled
NotImplemented in safe mode; a successful resolution with unsafe RPC enabled
A successful resolution in safe mode; UnavailableInSafeMode with unsafe RPC enabled
A successful resolution in both modes
questions.funFact: The handler first checks the safe-mode restriction, then explicitly returns NotImplemented. A request type or an unsafe-mode setting does not by itself establish that this operation is implemented.

questions.prompt: What does network_mempool_size sample in Rusty Kaspa's get_metrics_call implementation?
options: Every transaction waiting anywhere on the global Kaspa network
This node's non-orphan transactions in its ordinary mempool
Only this node's orphan transactions
All unspent outputs held by wallet addresses
questions.funFact: The value comes from this node's mining manager with TransactionsOnly. That query excludes the orphan pool; the network-prefixed field name does not make it a census of every node.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: Rusty Kaspa's get_metrics_call sets storage_size_bytes to zero when requested. What does this implementation show?
options: A verified absence of all stored blocks
Proof that pruning has removed every database file
A hard-coded value, not a measurement proving the database is empty
A coin amount that must be converted from sompi to KAS
questions.funFact: This Rusty Kaspa's service constructs the field with the literal value zero. Although the response model names a storage-size field, this implementation does not measure database usage for it.

questions.prompt: Which time basis does server_time in Rusty Kaspa's metrics response use?
options: Seconds since the node process started
The current virtual DAA score
The cumulative number of proof-of-work hashes
Milliseconds since the Unix epoch from the node's system clock
questions.funFact: The handler calls unix_now, whose definition returns SystemTime since UNIX_EPOCH in milliseconds. This timestamp is distinct from node uptime and the separately reported virtual DAA score.
